reviews.text: They measured the old spring before touching anything: wire size, length, inside diameter. The new pair is heavier wire, and the quote showed the cycle rating next to the price.
reviews.name: Agnieszka R.

reviews.text: Our detached garage on the alley still had the old stretch springs with no safety cable. Fixed in an afternoon. I did not know one of those could take out a windshield.
reviews.name: Brendan O.

reviews.text: Bottom panel was rusted through from twenty winters of road salt. They replaced one section instead of the door and put a new seal on. No more leaves in the garage.
reviews.name: Yvette H.

reviews.text: I asked about insulated doors and got three options with R-values side by side and real prices. Went with the middle one. The garage under our bedroom is noticeably warmer in January.
reviews.name: Sam D.

reviews.text: Opener died and I assumed I needed a new one. It was the travel-limit setting and a cracked gear. Fixed for a fraction of a new unit.
reviews.name: Ken L.

reviews.text: The maintenance sheet had actual numbers on it. Spring balance, opener force, which rollers had play. I keep it in the drawer with the furnace papers.
reviews.name: Rosa M.

reviews.text: Door reversed at random for a month. Tech put a two-by-four under it, adjusted force and moved one sensor bracket. Has not happened since.
reviews.name: Terrence J.

proof.guarantee: New springs are covered for the life of their rated cycles; labor on any repair for 1 year.
